newsitem.title: CROATIA: Britain's Rifkind says report on Mostar "shocking".
newsitem.headline: Britain's Rifkind says report on Mostar "shocking".

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Malcom Rifkind said on Wednesday he was shocked by a police report pinning the blame on Bosnian Croats for recent violence in the divided city of Mostar and demanded the culprits be brought to justice.
"This is a shocking report. It tells an appalling story," Rifkind said in a statement faxed to Reuters by the British Embassy in Zagreb.

"Those responsible must be brought to justice immediately," Rifkind said and called on the Croatian government to "use its influence with the Croat authorities in Mostar to ensure acceptance of the report".
International police investigators reported on Tuesday that Bosnian Croat police had fired on unarmed Moslems without cause and behaved in a criminal manner in the February 10 incident.
One Moslem man was killed and more than twenty wounded in the most serious violence to erupt since the Bosnian peace agreement was signed in December 1995.

The investigation, conducted by a team of monitors from the International Police Task Force (IPTF), said two Croat police were photographed firing into a crowd of retreating Moslems who had tried to visit a cemetery in Croat-held western Mostar.
Croat authorities have suspended six policemen over the incident but have also pressed charges against Moslems, alleging they provoked the violence.
The Mostar incident has damaged already strained relations within the Moslem-Croat federation, which together with the Serb republic comprises peacetime Bosnia.
